{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_c039784777dc4064926e8782","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-003: Cleanup Command Orphan-Detection Gap\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-19\n4\t**Deciders:** operator (jedarden), via Claude Code\n5\t**Tracking:** plan.md Phase 7; implementation beads in this repo's workspace (genesis TBD — see plan.md Phase 7)\n6\t\n7\t## Context\n8\t\n9\tFound during lab fleet remediation on 2026-07-19. Claude Code, acting on the operator's behalf, was auditing fleet productivity: worker `armor-p6a` (pinned to `~/ARMOR`) was confirmed genuinely productive; four workers pinned to `~/commitgraph` (`alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, `delta`) were either legitimately exhausted (no ready work) or burning cycles in an operator-gated re-verify loop; a roaming worker (`cgov`) was found stuck failing an orphaned-bead release call every ~17-minute idle cycle. The remediation plan was to stop the unproductive workers and relaunch fresh roaming ones.\n10\t\n11\tTwo things happened that didn't match the plan:\n12\t\n13\t1. `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` each reported `Stopped: needle-claude-code-glm-5-<name>`, but `ps aux` continued to show both underlying `needle run --workspace ~/commitgraph` processes running (PIDs 2244216 and 2248754) after the stop. This reproduces the exact defect plan.md §6.2 / ADR-002 \"Bug 2\" already describes and has planned — but not yet implemented — a fix for.\n14\t2. A subsequent bare `needle cleanup` (no `--all`, no `-i`, intended only to remove the now-orphaned tmux sessions for the workers just stopped) instead reported `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`. Neither was orphaned: `armor-p6a` had a live process actively executing (170+ accumulated CPU-hours at the time), and `needle-supervisor` was the fleet's own auto-scaling daemon. Both tmux sessions were destroyed. tmux's server process then exited on its own — `tmux list-sessions` reported `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default` — because tmux auto-terminates once its last session is gone. This read initially like a wider, unexplained incident; it was fully explained once the actual `cleanup` implementation was read.\n15\t\n16\tSource inspection (`src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`) found the root cause. `cmd_cleanup`'s own help text (`\"Remove orphaned tmux sessions (sessions without active workers)\"`) and doc comment (`\"Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\"`) both promise a liveness check. The implementation performs none:\n17\t\n18\t```rust\n19\tlet targets: Vec<&str> = if all {\n20\t    sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect()\n21\t} else {\n22\t    let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n23\t    sessions\n24\t        .iter()\n25\t        .filter(|s| id.is_empty() || s.name.contains(id))\n26\t        .map(|s| s.name.as_str())\n27\t        .collect()\n28\t};\n29\t```\n30\t\n31\tWhen called with neither `--all` nor `-i`, `identifier` is `None`, so `id` is `\"\"`, so `id.is_empty()` is always `true`, so every session matches the filter regardless of name. **Bare `needle cleanup` is functionally identical to `needle cleanup --all`.** No code path in `cmd_cleanup` calls `scan_needle_processes()` — the exact process-table reconciliation helper `cmd_list` already uses, and the one §6.2's exit criteria commits to building out for `needle status`/`needle list` — to check whether a session's registered PID actually corresponds to a live process. The command's own documentation describes a safety property that does not exist in the code.\n32\t\n33\tNet effect: `needle cleanup` is a hidden `--all` with extra steps whenever a caller omits `-i`, and its output (`Cleaned up: <name>`) is indistinguishable from a genuinely safe, scoped cleanup — there is no signal at the call site that anything destructive just happened to a live process.\n34\t\n35\t## Decision\n36\t\n37\t1. **Implement real liveness-based orphan detection as cleanup's default (no-flags) behavior.** A tmux session is a target only if `scan_needle_processes()` finds no live process backing its registered PID. Reuse this existing reconciliation helper rather than building a second, divergent liveness check — it is the same primitive §6.2 already commits to for `needle status`/`needle list`, so this ADR's fix and §6.2's fix should share one implementation once both land.\n38\t2. **`--all` keeps its current fully-destructive meaning, unchanged.** Its own `--help` text is updated to say so plainly (\"removes every needle session, including live ones\") so the danger is visible at the call site, not only in this design doc.\n39\t3. **`-i <pattern>` keeps its current targeted, deliberate meaning** — naming a specific session by pattern is itself the operator's explicit choice, so it continues to bypass the liveness check exactly as today. Only the no-flags path's behavior changes.\n40\t4. **Update `cmd_cleanup`'s help text and doc comment** to describe the behavior that will now actually exist, and add regression tests pinning all three paths (no-flags-live-preserved, no-flags-all-dead-noop, `--all`-unchanged) so the docs-vs-implementation gap that caused this incident cannot silently reopen.\n41\t5. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`) — per plan.md's established Deployment convention (§6.8).\n42\t\n43\t## Consequences\n44\t\n45\t- Bare `needle cleanup` becomes safe to run without a manual `ps aux` cross-check first — matches the same trust bar §6.2/ADR-002 already set for `needle stop`/`status`/`list`.\n46\t- No behavior change for `--all` (still fully destructive, now honestly documented) or `-i <name>` (still targeted/deliberate, unchanged).\n47\t- Cleanup's no-flags path now shells out to the same process-scan `cmd_list` already performs, rather than a single `tmux kill-session` loop over every registered name — bounded cost, only paid when cleanup is actually invoked.\n48\t- This fix's implementation depends on `scan_needle_processes()`-based reconciliation; if §6.2's landing slips, this ADR should ship its own minimal PID-liveness check rather than block on it, to avoid leaving the no-flags footgun live in the meantime.\n49\t- Does **not** fix the separate, already-tracked §6.2 defect (`needle stop` leaving orphaned processes behind after reporting success) — that remains open, and is in fact what produced the very \"orphaned\" sessions this bug then over-broadly swept up in the 2026-07-19 incident. The two defects compound: a not-fully-killed `needle stop` leaves a real orphan behind, but an unrelated live session sitting next to it in the tmux session list gets caught in the same net.\n50\t- `needle-supervisor` has no automatic restart-on-crash of its own; recovering from this incident required a fully manual relaunch. Worth a follow-up, not scoped to this ADR.\n51\t\n52\t## Evidence\n53\t\n54\t- `src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`, `cmd_cleanup` — full function reproduced above under Context; confirmed no liveness check exists in the `all == false` branch, and `sessions.iter().filter(|s| id.is_empty() || ...)` unconditionally matches everything when no `-i` is given.\n55\t- 2026-07-19 lab incident: `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` both reported `Stopped:` while `ps aux` continued to show `needle run --workspace /home/coding/commitgraph --identifier alpha` (PID 2244216) and the equivalent `delta` process (PID 2248754) alive, post-stop.\n56\t- 2026-07-19 lab incident: bare `needle cleanup` output — `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`, immediately followed by `tmux list-sessions` → `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default`. `armor-p6a`'s underlying process (PID 1421255, 170+ accumulated CPU-hours) survived independently of its tmux session and continued executing; Claude Code, acting on the operator's behalf, was auditing fleet productivity: worker `armor-p6a` (pinned to `~/ARMOR`) was confirmed genuinely productive; four workers pinned to `~/commitgraph` (`alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, `delta`) were either legitimately exhausted (no ready work) or burning cycles in an operator-gated re-verify loop; a roaming worker (`cgov`) was found stuck failing an orphaned-bead release call every ~17-minute idle cycle. The remediation plan was to stop the unproductive workers and relaunch fresh roaming ones.\n\nTwo things happened that didn't match the plan:\n\n1. `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` each reported `Stopped: needle-claude-code-glm-5-<name>`, but `ps aux` continued to show both underlying `needle run --workspace ~/commitgraph` processes running (PIDs 2244216 and 2248754) after the stop. This reproduces the exact defect plan.md §6.2 / ADR-002 \"Bug 2\" already describes and has planned — but not yet implemented — a fix for.\n2. A subsequent bare `needle cleanup` (no `--all`, no `-i`, intended only to remove the now-orphaned tmux sessions for the workers just stopped) instead reported `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`. Neither was orphaned: `armor-p6a` had a live process actively executing (170+ accumulated CPU-hours at the time), and `needle-supervisor` was the fleet's own auto-scaling daemon. Both tmux sessions were destroyed. tmux's server process then exited on its own — `tmux list-sessions` reported `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default` — because tmux auto-terminates once its last session is gone. This read initially like a wider, unexplained incident; it was fully explained once the actual `cleanup` implementation was read.\n\nSource inspection (`src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`) found the root cause. `cmd_cleanup`'s own help text (`\"Remove orphaned tmux sessions (sessions without active workers)\"`) and doc comment (`\"Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\"`) both promise a liveness check. The implementation performs none:\n\n```rust\nlet targets: Vec<&str> = if all {\n    sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect()\n} else {\n    let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    sessions\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|s| id.is_empty() || s.name.contains(id))\n        .map(|s| s.name.as_str())\n        .collect()\n};\n```\n\nWhen called with neither `--all` nor `-i`, `identifier` is `None`, so `id` is `\"\"`, so `id.is_empty()` is always `true`, so every session matches the filter regardless of name. **Bare `needle cleanup` is functionally identical to `needle cleanup --all`.** No code path in `cmd_cleanup` calls `scan_needle_processes()` — the exact process-table reconciliation helper `cmd_list` already uses, and the one §6.2's exit criteria commits to building out for `needle status`/`needle list` — to check whether a session's registered PID actually corresponds to a live process. The command's own documentation describes a safety property that does not exist in the code.\n\nNet effect: `needle cleanup` is a hidden `--all` with extra steps whenever a caller omits `-i`, and its output (`Cleaned up: <name>`) is indistinguishable from a genuinely safe, scoped cleanup — there is no signal at the call site that anything destructive just happened to a live process.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **Implement real liveness-based orphan detection as cleanup's default (no-flags) behavior.** A tmux session is a target only if `scan_needle_processes()` finds no live process backing its registered PID. Reuse this existing reconciliation helper rather than building a second, divergent liveness check — it is the same primitive §6.2 already commits to for `needle status`/`needle list`, so this ADR's fix and §6.2's fix should share one implementation once both land.\n2. **`--all` keeps its current fully-destructive meaning, unchanged.** Its own `--help` text is updated to say so plainly (\"removes every needle session, including live ones\") so the danger is visible at the call site, not only in this design doc.\n3. **`-i <pattern>` keeps its current targeted, deliberate meaning** — naming a specific session by pattern is itself the operator's explicit choice, so it continues to bypass the liveness check exactly as today. Only the no-flags path's behavior changes.\n4. **Update `cmd_cleanup`'s help text and doc comment** to describe the behavior that will now actually exist, and add regression tests pinning all three paths (no-flags-live-preserved, no-flags-all-dead-noop, `--all`-unchanged) so the docs-vs-implementation gap that caused this incident cannot silently reopen.\n5. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`) — per plan.md's established Deployment convention (§6.8).\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Bare `needle cleanup` becomes safe to run without a manual `ps aux` cross-check first — matches the same trust bar §6.2/ADR-002 already set for `needle stop`/`status`/`list`.\n- No behavior change for `--all` (still fully destructive, now honestly documented) or `-i <name>` (still targeted/deliberate, unchanged).\n- Cleanup's no-flags path now shells out to the same process-scan `cmd_list` already performs, rather than a single `tmux kill-session` loop over every registered name — bounded cost, only paid when cleanup is actually invoked.\n- This fix's implementation depends on `scan_needle_processes()`-based reconciliation; if §6.2's landing slips, this ADR should ship its own minimal PID-liveness check rather than block on it, to avoid leaving the no-flags footgun live in the meantime.\n- Does **not** fix the separate, already-tracked §6.2 defect (`needle stop` leaving orphaned processes behind after reporting success) — that remains open, and is in fact what produced the very \"orphaned\" sessions this bug then over-broadly swept up in the 2026-07-19 incident. The two defects compound: a not-fully-killed `needle stop` leaves a real orphan behind, but an unrelated live session sitting next to it in the tmux session list gets caught in the same net.\n- `needle-supervisor` has no automatic restart-on-crash of its own; recovering from this incident required a fully manual relaunch. Worth a follow-up, not scoped to this ADR.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `src/cli/mod.rs:1435-1487`, `cmd_cleanup` — full function reproduced above under Context; confirmed no liveness check exists in the `all == false` branch, and `sessions.iter().filter(|s| id.is_empty() || ...)` unconditionally matches everything when no `-i` is given.\n- 2026-07-19 lab incident: `needle stop -i alpha` and `needle stop -i delta` both reported `Stopped:` while `ps aux` continued to show `needle run --workspace /home/coding/commitgraph --identifier alpha` (PID 2244216) and the equivalent `delta` process (PID 2248754) alive, post-stop.\n- 2026-07-19 lab incident: bare `needle cleanup` output — `Cleaned up: needle-claude-code-glm-5-armor-p6a` and `Cleaned up: needle-supervisor`, immediately followed by `tmux list-sessions` → `no server running on /tmp/tmux-1001/default`. `armor-p6a`'s underlying process (PID 1421255, 170+ accumulated CPU-hours) survived independently of its tmux session and continued executing; ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n351\t// Entry point\n352\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n353\t\n354\t/// Entry point called from `main`.\n355\tpub fn run() -> Result<()> {\n356\t    let cli = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n420\t\n421\t/// `needle run` — launch a worker.\n422\t///\n423\t/// Always creates dedicated tmux sessions for workers, even when invoked from\n424\t/// inside an existing tmux session. The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n425\t/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n426\t/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\n427\tfn cmd_run(\n428\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n429\t    agent: Option<String>,\n430\t    count: u32,\n431\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n432\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n433\t    resume: bool,\n434\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n435\t) -> Result<()> {\n436\t    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n437\t    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n438\t        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n439\t    } else {\n440\t        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n441\t        global.workspace.default.clone()\n442\t    };\n443\t\n444\t    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n445\t    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n446\t        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n447\t        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n448\t        max_workers: None,\n449\t        ..Default::default()\n450\t    };\n451\t    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n452\t\n453\t    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n454\t        config.agent.timeout = t;\n455\t    }\n456\t\n457\t    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n458\t        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n459\t    }\n460\t\n461\t    if resume {\n462\t        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n463\t        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n464\t        let worker_id = identifier\n465\t            .clone()\n466\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n467\t\n468\t        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n469\t        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n470\t\n471\t        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n472\t        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n473\t            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n474\t        )\n475\t        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n476\t\n477\t        match &resume_state {\n478\t            Some(state) => {\n479\t                tracing::info!(\n480\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n481\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n482\t                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n483\t                    session = %state.session,\n484\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n485\t                );\n486\t            }\n487\t            None => {\n488\t                tracing::info!(\n489\t                    worker = %worker_id,\n490\t                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n491\t                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n492\t                );\n493\t            }\n494\t        }\n495\t\n496\t        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n497\t            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n498\t                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n499\t                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n500\t            });\n501\t        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n502\t            new_hash: current_hash,\n503\t        })?;\n504\t\n505\t        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n506\t    }\n507\t\n508\t    if is_needle_inner() {\n509\t        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n510\t        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n511\t        let worker_id = identifier\n512\t            .clone()\n513\t            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n514\t        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n515\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n516\t        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n517\t        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n518\t    } else {\n519\t        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n520\t        launch_workers(\n521\t            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n522\t        )\n523\t    }\n524\t}\n525\t\n526\t/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\n527\tpub fn launch_workers(\n528\t    config: Config,\n529\t    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n530\t    agent: Option<String>,\n531\t    count: u32,\n532\t    identifier: Option<String>,\n533\t    timeout: Option<u64>,\n534\t    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n535\t) -> Result<()> {\n536\t    let agent_name = agent\n537\t        .as_deref()\n538\t        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n539\t        .to_string();\n540\t    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n541\t    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n542\t\n543\t    if count == 0 {\n544\t        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n545\t    }\n546\t    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n547\t        bail!(\n548\t            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n549\t            count,\n550\t            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n551\t        );\n552\t    }\n553\t\n554\t    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n555\t    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n556\t        tracing::warn!(\n557\t            requested = count,\n558\t            capped_to = max_workers,\n559\t            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n560\t        );\n561\t        eprintln!(\n562\t            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n563\t        );\n564\t        max_workers\n565\t    } else {\n566\t        count\n567\t    };\n568\t\n569\t    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n570\t    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n571\t        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n572\t    }\n573\t\n574\t    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n575\t    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n576\t    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n577\t        tracing::info!(\n578\t            occupied = ?occupied,\n579\t            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n580\t        );\n581\t    }\n582\t\n583\t    // Reject --identifier collision early.\n584\t    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n585\t        if occupied.contains(id) {\n586\t            bail!(\n587\t                \"worker '{}' is already running in session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n588\t                id,\n589\t                agent_name,\n590\t                id\n591\t            );\n592\t        }\n593\t    }\n594\t\n595\t    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n596\t    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n597\t        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n598\t            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n599\t            NATO_ALPHABET\n600\t                .iter()\n601\t                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n602\t                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n603\t                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n604\t        })]\n605\t    } else {\n606\t        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n607\t        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n608\t            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n609\t                break;\n610\t            }\n611\t            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n612\t                tracing::warn!(\n613\t                    worker_id = %name,\n614\t                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n615\t                );\n616\t                continue;\n617\t            }\n618\t            ids.push(name.to_string());\n619\t        }\n620\t        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n621\t            bail!(\n622\t                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n623\t                effective_count,\n624\t                ids.len(),\n625\t                occupied.len()\n626\t            );\n627\t        }\n628\t        ids\n629\t    };\n630\t\n631\t    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n632\t        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n633\t\n634\t        tracing::info!(\n635\t            worker_id = %worker_id,\n636\t            sequence = seq,\n637\t            total = effective_count,\n638\t            session = %session_name,\n639\t            \"launching worker\"\n640\t        );\n641\t\n642\t        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n643\t        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n644\t            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n645\t        }\n646\t\n647\t        launch_in_tmux(\n648\t            &session_name,\n649\t            workspace.clone(),\n650\t            agent.clone(),\n651\t            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n652\t            timeout,\n653\t            hot_reload,\n654\t        )?;\n655\t\n656\t        println!(\n657\t            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n658\t            seq + 1,\n659\t            effective_count,\n660\t            worker_id\n661\t        );\n662\t    }\n663\t\n664\t    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n665\t    if effective_count > 1 {\n666\t        println!(\n667\t            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n668\t        );\n669\t        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n670\t    } else {\n671\t        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n672\t        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n673\t    }\n674\t\n675\t    Ok(())\n676\t}\n677\t\n678\t/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n679\t///\n680\t/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n681\t/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n682\t///\n683\t/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n684\t#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\n685\tfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n686\t    worker_id: String,\n687\t    session_id: String,\n688\t    config: &crate::config::Config,\n689\t) -> Result<()> {\n690\t    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n691\t    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n692\t\n693\t    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n694\t\n695\t    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n696\t    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n697\t        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n698\t        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n699\t            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n700\t            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n701\t        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n702\t            .with(fmt_layer)\n703\t            .try_init()\n704\t            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n705\t        return Ok(());\n706\t    }\n707\t\n708\t    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n709\t    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n710\t    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n711\t\n712\t    // Build resource attributes\n713\t    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n714\t        &worker_id,\n715\t        &session_id,\n716\t        otlp_config,\n717\t        Some(&config.agent.default),\n718\t        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n719\t        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n720\t    )\n721\t    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n722\t\n723\t    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n724\t    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n725\t        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n726\t    tokio::spawn(async move {\n727\t        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n728\t            tracing::warn!(\n729\t                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n730\t                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n731\t                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n732\t            );\n733\t        }\n734\t    });\n735\t\n736\t    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n737\t    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n738\t        \"grpc\" => {\n739\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n740\t        }\n741\t        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n742\t            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n743\t        }\n744\t        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n745\t    };\n746\t\n747\t    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n748\t    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n749\t\n750\t    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n751\t    // We build this ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Command handlers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `needle run` — launch a worker.\n///\n/// Always creates dedicated tmux sessions for workers, even when invoked from\n/// inside an existing tmux session. The only exception is a re-entrant inner\n/// invocation launched by `launch_in_tmux()`, which is identified by the\n/// `NEEDLE_INNER=1` environment variable and runs the worker directly.\nfn cmd_run(\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    resume: bool,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Determine workspace root (CLI arg → canonicalized, else global default).\n    let workspace_root = if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        ws.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| ws.clone())\n    } else {\n        let global = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n        global.workspace.default.clone()\n    };\n\n    // Load full resolved config (global → workspace .needle.yaml → env → CLI).\n    let cli_overrides = CliOverrides {\n        workspace: Some(workspace_root.clone()),\n        agent_binary: agent.clone(),\n        max_workers: None,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let (mut config, _) = ConfigLoader::load_resolved(&workspace_root, cli_overrides)?;\n\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        config.agent.timeout = t;\n    }\n\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        config.self_modification.hot_reload = hr;\n    }\n\n    if resume {\n        // Hot-reload resume: inherit worker identity from --identifier,\n        // load state from heartbeat file + registry, continue from SELECTING.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n\n        // Load resume state from heartbeat and registry.\n        let resume_state = crate::upgrade::ResumeState::load(&config, &worker_id)?;\n\n        // Emit upgrade.completed telemetry.\n        let current_hash = crate::upgrade::file_hash(\n            &std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?,\n        )\n        .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"unknown\".to_string());\n\n        match &resume_state {\n            Some(state) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    beads_processed = state.beads_processed,\n                    session = %state.session,\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload\"\n                );\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    worker = %worker_id,\n                    binary_hash = %&current_hash[..current_hash.len().min(12)],\n                    \"resuming worker after hot-reload (no prior state found)\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        let tel = crate::telemetry::Telemetry::from_config(worker_id.clone(), &config.telemetry)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"hook telemetry init failed, falling back\");\n                crate::telemetry::Telemetry::new(worker_id.clone())\n            });\n        tel.emit(crate::telemetry::EventKind::UpgradeCompleted {\n            new_hash: current_hash,\n        })?;\n\n        return run_worker(config, worker_id);\n    }\n\n    if is_needle_inner() {\n        // Re-entrant inner invocation launched by launch_in_tmux() — run\n        // the worker directly inside the dedicated session already created.\n        let worker_id = identifier\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string());\n        let agent_name = agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(&config.agent.default);\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n        tracing::info!(worker = %worker_id, session = %session_name, \"starting worker (inner re-entrant invocation)\");\n        run_worker(config, worker_id)\n    } else {\n        // Always create dedicated tmux sessions, even if already inside tmux.\n        launch_workers(\n            config, workspace, agent, count, identifier, timeout, hot_reload,\n        )\n    }\n}\n\n/// Launch `count` workers in separate tmux sessions with staggered startup delays.\npub fn launch_workers(\n    config: Config,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    count: u32,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let agent_name = agent\n        .as_deref()\n        .unwrap_or(&config.agent.default)\n        .to_string();\n    let stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds;\n    let max_workers = config.worker.max_workers;\n\n    if count == 0 {\n        bail!(\"--count must be at least 1\");\n    }\n    if count as usize > NATO_ALPHABET.len() {\n        bail!(\n            \"--count {} exceeds the maximum of {} (NATO alphabet size)\",\n            count,\n            NATO_ALPHABET.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Enforce max_workers cap (0 means unlimited).\n    let effective_count = if max_workers > 0 && count > max_workers {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            requested = count,\n            capped_to = max_workers,\n            \"count exceeds max_workers; capping\"\n        );\n        eprintln!(\n            \"Warning: --count {count} exceeds max_workers={max_workers}; launching {max_workers} workers\"\n        );\n        max_workers\n    } else {\n        count\n    };\n\n    // --identifier is only meaningful for a single worker.\n    if effective_count > 1 && identifier.is_some() {\n        bail!(\"--identifier cannot be combined with --count > 1; identifiers are auto-assigned from the NATO alphabet\");\n    }\n\n    // Detect existing sessions to avoid name collisions.\n    let occupied = occupied_worker_ids(&agent_name)?;\n    if !occupied.is_empty() {\n        tracing::info!(\n            occupied = ?occupied,\n            \"found existing worker sessions\"\n        );\n session 'needle-{}-{}'\",\n                id,\n                agent_name,\n                id\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Build the list of worker IDs, skipping occupied names.\n    let worker_ids: Vec<String> = if effective_count == 1 {\n        vec![identifier.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {\n            // Pick the first available NATO name.\n            NATO_ALPHABET\n                .iter()\n                .find(|name| !occupied.contains(**name))\n                .map(|s| s.to_string())\n                .unwrap_or_else(|| NATO_ALPHABET[0].to_string())\n        })]\n    } else {\n        let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(effective_count as usize);\n        for name in NATO_ALPHABET {\n            if ids.len() >= effective_count as usize {\n                break;\n            }\n            if occupied.contains(*name) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id = %name,\n                    \"skipping occupied worker name\"\n                );\n                continue;\n            }\n            ids.push(name.to_string());\n        }\n        if ids.len() < effective_count as usize {\n            bail!(\n                \"cannot launch {} workers — only {} NATO names available ({} occupied)\",\n                effective_count,\n                ids.len(),\n                occupied.len()\n            );\n        }\n        ids\n    };\n\n    for (seq, worker_id) in worker_ids.iter().enumerate() {\n        let session_name = sanitize_session_name(&format!(\"needle-{agent_name}-{worker_id}\"));\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            worker_id = %worker_id,\n            sequence = seq,\n            total = effective_count,\n            session = %session_name,\n            \"launching worker\"\n        );\n\n        // Stagger: sleep before launching subsequent workers.\n        if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 {\n            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs));\n        }\n\n        launch_in_tmux(\n            &session_name,\n            workspace.clone(),\n            agent.clone(),\n            Some(worker_id.clone()),\n            timeout,\n            hot_reload,\n        )?;\n\n        println!(\n            \"[{}/{}] Started worker '{}' in tmux session: {session_name}\",\n            seq + 1,\n            effective_count,\n            worker_id\n        );\n    }\n\n    let sanitized_agent = sanitize_session_name(&agent_name);\n    if effective_count > 1 {\n        println!(\n            \"\\nStarted {effective_count} workers (stagger: {stagger_secs}s between launches).\"\n        );\n        println!(\"Attach to a worker with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-<name>\");\n    } else {\n        let worker_id = &worker_ids[0];\n        println!(\"Attach with: tmux attach -t needle-{sanitized_agent}-{worker_id}\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Initialize the tracing subscriber with OTLP layer if configured.\n///\n/// This must be called before any tracing spans are created so that the OTLP\n/// layer can export them to the configured collector.\n///\n/// Note: Shutdown is handled by the OtlpSink in the telemetry module, not here.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    worker_id: String,\n    session_id: String,\n    config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TracerProvider;\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Check if OTLP is enabled\n    if !config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled {\n        // No OTLP - just initialize with fmt layer\n        let fmt_layer = tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi);\n        tracing_subscriber::registry()\n            .with(fmt_layer)\n            .try_init()\n            .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // OTLP is enabled - create the OTLP layer inline\n    // We create it inline to avoid type erasure issues with boxed layers\n    let otlp_config = &config.telemetry.otlp_sink;\n\n    // Build resource attributes\n    let resource = crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_resource(\n        &worker_id,\n        &session_id,\n        otlp_config,\n        Some(&config.agent.default),\n        None, // model - not available in AgentConfig\n        config.workspace.default.to_str(),\n    )\n    .context(\"failed to build OTel resource\")?;\n\n    // Create drop channel for tracing layer\n    let (drop_tx, mut drop_rx) =\n        tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<crate::telemetry::otlp::DropEvent>();\n    tokio::spawn(async move {\n        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                signal = drop.signal.as_str(),\n                dropped_count = drop.dropped_count,\n                \"OTLP tracing layer export failure\"\n            );\n        }\n    });\n\n    // Build exporters and tracer provider based on protocol\n    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match otlp_config.protocol.as_str() {\n        \"grpc\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => {\n            crate::telemetry::otlp::OtlpSink::build_http_providers(otlp_config, &resource, drop_tx)?\n        }\n        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n    };\n\n    // Create the OpenTelemetry tracing layer\n    let otlp_layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n\n    // Create a fmt layer that works with any subscriber implementing LookupSpan\n    // We build this after the OTLP layer to ensure proper type compatibility\n    let subscriber = tracing_subscriber::registry().with(otlp_layer).with(\n        tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n            .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n            .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n    );\n\n    subscriber\n        .try_init()\n        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber with OTLP\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// No-op tracing initialization when OTLP feature is disabled.\n#[cfg(not(feature = \"otlp\"))]\nfn init_tracing_subscriber(\n    _worker_id: String,\n    _session_id: String,\n    _config: &crate::config::Config,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    use tracing_subscriber::{layer::SubscriberExt, util::SubscriberInitExt};\n\n    let use_ansi = use_ansi();\n\n    // Initialize with just the stdout layer when OTLP is disabled\n    tracing_subscriber::registry()\n        .with(\n            tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer()\n                .with_writer(std::io::stderr)\n                .with_ansi(use_ansi),\n        )\n        .try_init()\n        .context(\"failed to initialize tracing subscriber\")?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Helper function to determine ANSI support (non-Android platforms).\n#[cfg(not(target_os = \"android\"))]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    atty::is(atty::Stream::Stderr)\n}\n\n/// Helper function for Android (no ANSI).\n#[cfg(target_os = \"android\")]\nfn use_ansi() -> bool {\n    false\n}\n\n/// Generate a session ID for a worker.\n///\n/// Uses the telemetry module's session ID generator.\nfn generate_session_id_for_worker() -> String {\n    crate::telemetry::generate_session_id()\n}\n\n/// Start the worker state machine (called when inside tmux or for direct mode).\n///\n/// Creates telemetry and the tokio runtime *before* any other initialization\n/// so that `worker.booting` is the very first JSONL event. Each subsequent\n/// init step is wrapped with `init.step.started` / `init.step.completed` so a\n/// silent hang pinpoints the exact blocking call.\nfn run_worker(config: Config, worker_name: String) -> Result<()> {\n    let boot_start = Instant::now();\n    let qualified_id = format!(\"{}-{}\", config.agent.default, worker_name);\n\n    // Phase 0: create tokio runtime + telemetry, emit worker.booting immediately.\n    // Emit eprintln diagnostics before each step so hangs are visible even if telemetry fails.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...\");\n    let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context(\"failed to create tokio runtime\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...\");\n    let session_id = generate_session_id_for_worker();\n    init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: tracing subscriber initialized\");\n\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: creating telemetry...\");\n    let telemetry =\n        Telemetry::from_config(qualified_id.clone(), &config.telemetry).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n            tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"failed to create hook-enabled telemetry, falling back\");\n            Telemetry::new(qualified_id.clone())\n        });\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: telemetry created\");\n\n    // Emit worker.booting SYNCHRONOUSLY before starting the async writer.\n    // This guarantees the event is written to disk even if start_and_wait() hangs.\n    // Fixes the silent pre-init deadlock where the JSONL file is created but empty.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: emitting worker.booting event (sync)...\");\n    telemetry.emit_sync(EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n        worker_name: worker_name.clone(),\n        version: env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string(),\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: worker.booting written to disk\");\n\n    // Start the async writer thread after worker.booting is on disk.\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting telemetry writer thread...\");\n    rt.block_on(telemetry.start_and_wait())\n        .context(\"writer thread failed to start\")?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: writer thread started\");\n\n    // Phase 1: bead store discovery.\n    // Use BfCliBeadStore for atomic server-selected bead claiming.\n    let store: Arc<dyn crate::bead_store::BeadStore> =\n        Arc::new(init_step(\"bead_store_discover\", &telemetry, || {\n            let bf_store = crate::bead_store::BfCliBeadStore::discover(\n                config.workspace.default.clone(),\n                None,                       // model: do not filter by model — beads are untagged\n                Some(\"needle\".to_string()), // harness\n                Some(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\").to_string()), // harness_version\n            )\n            .context(\"failed to locate bf CLI for bead store\")?;\n\n            // Run bead-forge version handshake to detect known-bad versions.\n            let bf_path = &bf_store.bf_path;\n            let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()\n                .context(\"failed to create runtime for version check\")?;\n            rt.block_on(crate::bead_store::run_version_handshake(bf_path));\n\n            Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(bf_store)\n        })?);\n\n    // Phase 2: worker construction (heavy — prompt loading, adapter discovery, etc.).\n    let mut worker = init_step(\"worker_construction\", &telemetry, || {\n        Ok(Worker::new_with_telemetry(\n            config,\n            worker_name.clone(),\n            store,\n            telemetry.clone(),\n        ))\n    })?;\n\n    // Boot timeout guard: self-abort if init took >60 s.\n    let elapsed_ms = boot_start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    if elapsed_ms > 60_000 {\n        telemetry.emit(EventKind::WorkerBootTimeout { elapsed_ms })?;\n        bail!(\"boot exceeded 60 s ({elapsed_ms} ms), aborting\");\n    }\n\n    eprintln!(\n        \"NEEDLE worker boot: all init steps completed in {elapsed_ms}ms, starting worker loop...\"\n    );\n    let result = rt.block_on(worker.run())?;\n\n    tracing::info!(final_state = %result, \"worker finished\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Emit start/complete telemetry around a fallible initialization step.\n///\n/// Each step's completion is force-flushed to disk so that if a subsequent\n/// step blocks indefinitely, the telemetry log shows exactly where it stopped.\n/// Also emits eprintln diagnostics for visibility even if telemetry hangs.\nfn init_step<T, F>(name: &str, tel: &Telemetry, f: F) -> Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: FnOnce() -> Result<T>,\n{\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: starting init step '{name}'...\");\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepStarted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let t = Instant::now();\n    let result = f();\n    let elapsed = t.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;\n    tel.emit(EventKind::InitStepCompleted {\n        step: name.to_string(),\n        duration_ms: elapsed,\n    })?;\n    eprintln!(\"NEEDLE worker boot: init step '{name}' completed in {elapsed}ms\");\n    // Force-flush so the step completion is visible before the next (potentially blocking) step.\n    tel.force_flush(std::time::Duration::from_secs(1))?;\n    result\n}\n\n/// Returns true when this process is a re-entrant inner invocation launched\n/// by `launch_in_tmux()`, indicated by `NEEDLE_INNER=1` in the environment.\nfn is_needle_inner() -> bool {\n    std::env::var(\"NEEDLE_INNER\").is_ok_and(|v| v == \"1\")\n}\n\n/// Create a single tmux session and re-exec self inside it with `--count 1`.\nfn launch_in_tmux(\n    session_name: &str,\n    workspace: Option<PathBuf>,\n    agent: Option<String>,\n    identifier: Option<String>,\n    timeout: Option<u64>,\n    hot_reload: Option<bool>,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    // Build the command that tmux will run inside the session.\n    let self_exe = std::env::current_exe().context(\"failed to locate own binary\")?;\n    let mut inner_args = vec![\"run\".to_string()];\n\n    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace {\n        inner_args.push(\"--workspace\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(ws.display().to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(ref a) = agent {\n        inner_args.push(\"--agent\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(a.clone());\n    }\n    // Each session runs exactly one worker; identifier is always resolved before call.\n    inner_args.push(\"--count\".to_string());\n    inner_args.push(\"1\".to_string());\n    if let Some(ref id) = identifier {\n        inner_args.push(\"--identifier\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(id.clone());\n    }\n    if let Some(t) = timeout {\n        inner_args.push(\"--timeout\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(t.to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(hr) = hot_reload {\n        inner_args.push(\"--hot-reload\".to_string());\n        inner_args.push(hr.to_string());\n    }\n\n    // Build stderr log path: ~/.needle/logs/<session_name>.stderr.log\n    let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n    let stderr_log = format!(\"{home}/.needle/logs/{session_name}.stderr.log\");\n\n    let inner_cmd = format!(\n        \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 {} {} 2>> {}\",\n        shell_escape(&self_exe.display().to_string()),\n        inner_args\n            .iter()\n            .map(|a| shell_escape(a))\n            .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            .join(\" \"),\n        shell_escape(&stderr_log)\n    );\n\n    let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n        .args([\"new-session\", \"-d\", \"-s\", session_name, &inner_cmd])\n        .status()\n        .context(\"failed to launch tmux — is tmux installed?\")?;\n\n    if !status.success() {\n        bail!(\n            \"tmux new-session exited with status {} for session '{}'\",\n            status,\n            session_name\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Kill the entire process tree rooted at the given PID.\n///\n/// This function recursively finds all child processes and sends SIGTERM,\n/// waits for processes to exit, and sends SIGKILL to any remaining processes.\n/// Returns true if all processes were successfully terminated.\n///\n/// This is necessary because agents are spawned with setpgid(0,0), creating\n/// new process groups that are not reachable via killpg() on the parent PGID.\nfn kill_process_tree(pid: u32) -> Result<bool> {\n    use std::thread;\n\n    tracing::info!(pid, \"finding all descendant processes to terminate\");\n\n    // Collect all descendant PIDs by reading /proc\n    let descendants = find_all_descendants(pid);\n    let descendant_count = descendants.len();\n\n    if descendant_count > 0 {\n        tracing::info!(\n            pid,\n            count = descendant_count,\n            ?descendants,\n            \"found descendant processes\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Send SIGTERM to all descendants (including the original PID)\n    let all_pids: Vec<u32> = std::iter::once(pid).chain(descendants).collect();\n    tracing::info!(\n        pid,\n        count = all_pids.len(),\n        \"sending SIGTERM to process tree\"\n    );\n\n    for target_pid in &all_pids {\n        unsafe {\n            if libc::kill(*target_pid as libc::pid_t, libc::SIGTERM) == -1 {\n                let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();\n                if err.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {\n                    tracing::warn!(pid = target_pid, error = %err, \"SIGTERM failed\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Wait up to 5 seconds for processes to exit gracefully\n    for i in 0..50 {\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n\n        // Check if all processes are gone\n        let all_dead = all_pids\n            .iter()\n            .all(|&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) != 0 });\n\n        if all_dead {\n            tracing::info!(\n                pid,\n                \"process tree terminated gracefully after {}ms\",\n                (i + 1) * 100\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Some processes survived SIGTERM, use SIGKILL\n    tracing::warn!(pid, \"process tree survived SIGTERM, sending SIGKILL\");\n    for target_pid in &all_pids {\n        unsafe {\n            if libc::kill(*target_pid as libc::pid_t, libc::SIGKILL) == -1 {\n                let err = std::io::Error::last_os_error();\n                if err.kind() != std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {\n                    tracing::error!(pid = target_pid, error = %err, \"SIGKILL failed\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Wait up to 3 seconds for SIGKILL to take effect\n    for i in 0..30 {\n        thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));\n\n        let all_dead = all_pids\n            .iter()\n            .all(|&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) != 0 });\n\n        if all_dead {\n            tracing::info!(\n                pid,\n                \"process tree terminated by SIGKILL after {}ms\",\n                (i + 1) * 100\n            );\n            return Ok(true);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Check which processes are still alive\n    let still_alive: Vec<u32> = all_pids\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|&&p| unsafe { libc::kill(p as libc::pid_t, 0) == 0 })\n        .copied()\n        .collect();\n\n    if !still_alive.is_empty() {\n        tracing::error!(\n            pid,\n            ?still_alive,\n            \"process tree survived SIGKILL - {} processes still running\",\n            still_alive.len()\n        );\n    }\n\n    Ok(still_alive.is_empty())\n}\n\n/// Recursively find all descendant processes of the given PID.\n///\n/// Reads /proc to build a process tree and returns all descendant PIDs.\n/// This handles the case where agents create new process groups with setpgid(0,0).\nfn find_all_descendants(root_pid: u32) -> Vec<u32> {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let proc_dir = Path::new(\"/proc\");\n    let mut ppid_to_children: HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>> = HashMap::new();\n\n    // First pass: build parent->children mapping\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(proc_dir) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            let pid_str = entry.file_name();\n            let pid: u32 = match pid_str.to_string_lossy().parse() {\n                Ok(p) => p,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Skip the root PID itself\n            if pid == root_pid {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Read /proc/[pid]/status to get PPID\n            let status_path = entry.path().join(\"status\");\n            if let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&status_path) {\n                let ppid = content\n                    .lines()\n                    .find(|line| line.starts_with(\"PPID:\\t\"))\n                    .and_then(|line| line.split(':').nth(1))\n                    .and_then(|v| v.trim().parse().ok());\n\n                if let Some(parent_pid) = ppid {\n                    ppid_to_children.entry(parent_pid).or_default().push(pid);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Recursive DFS to find all descendants\n    let mut descendants = Vec::new();\n    let mut visited = HashSet::new();\n    // Mark the root PID as visited to prevent cycles\n    visited.insert(root_pid);\n    find_descendants_recursive(root_pid, &ppid_to_children, &mut descendants, &mut visited);\n\n    descendants\n}\n\n/// Recursive helper to traverse process tree and collect descendants.\nfn find_descendants_recursive(\n    pid: u32,\n    ppid_to_children: &HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>>,\n    descendants: &mut Vec<u32>,\n    visited: &mut HashSet<u32>,\n) {\n    if let Some(children) = ppid_to_children.get(&pid) {\n        for &child_pid in children {\n            if visited.insert(child_pid) {\n                descendants.push(child_pid);\n                find_descendants_recursive(child_pid, ppid_to_children, descendants, visited);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a PID is a needle run process by reading /proc/[pid]/cmdline.\n///\n/// Returns true if the process command line contains \"needle run\".\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn is_needle_run_process(pid: u32) -> bool {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let cmdline_path = Path::new(\"/proc\").join(pid.to_string()).join(\"cmdline\");\n    let cmdline_bytes = match fs::read(&cmdline_path) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(_) => return false, // Process may have exited or /proc not available\n    };\n\n    // cmdline is null-separated; convert to space-separated for checking.\n    let cmdline: String = cmdline_bytes\n        .split(|&b| b == 0)\n        .map(|args| String::from_utf8_lossy(args))\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n        .join(\" \");\n\n    cmdline.contains(\"needle run\")\n}\n\n/// Find the actual needle run process in a process tree.\n///\n/// Given a root PID (typically from tmux pane_pid), this function searches for\n/// needle run processes in the descendant tree. This handles the case where\n/// tmux pane_pid returns a shell PID instead of the actual needle binary.\n///\n/// Returns the PID of the needle run process if found, None otherwise.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn find_needle_process_in_tree(root_pid: u32) -> Option<u32> {\n    // First check if the root itself is a needle run process\n    if is_needle_run_process(root_pid) {\n        return Some(root_pid);\n    }\n\n    // Search descendants for needle run processes\n    let descendants = find_all_descendants(root_pid);\n    descendants\n        .into_iter()\n        .find(|&pid| is_needle_run_process(pid))\n}\n\n/// Check if any needle processes are still running after a kill attempt.\n///\n/// This function scans the process table to find all needle run processes\n/// and their descendants. This is used after a kill attempt to verify that\n/// ALL processes (needle run + dispatched agent + any descendants) are\n/// actually gone, not just the original PID we tried to kill.\n///\n/// Returns a vector of PIDs that are still running, along with their command lines.\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn verify_no_needle_processes_remaining() -> Vec<(u32, String)> {\n    use std::fs;\n\n    let proc_dir = Path::new(\"/proc\");\n    let mut remaining = Vec::new();\n\n    if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(proc_dir) {\n        for entry in entries.flatten() {\n            let pid_str = entry.file_name();\n            let pid: u32 = match pid_str.to_string_lossy().parse() {\n                Ok(p) => p,\n                Err(_) => continue,\n            };\n\n            // Read /proc/[pid]/cmdline to check if this is a needle process\n            let cmdline_path = entry.path().join(\"cmdline\");\n            let cmdline_bytes = match fs::read(&cmdline_path) {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(_) => continue, // Process may have exited\n            };\n\n            // cmdline is null-separated; convert to space-separated for checking.\n            let cmdline: String = cmdline_bytes\n                .split(|&b| b == 0)\n                .map(|args| String::from_utf8_lossy(args))\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\" \");\n\n            // Check if this is a needle run process or a related subprocess\n            if cmdline.contains(\"needle run\") || cmdline.contains(\"NEEDLE_INNER\") {\n                remaining.push((pid, cmdline));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    remaining\n}\n\n/// `needle stop` — kill the full process tree for worker processes.\n///\n/// This command kills the parent needle run process, its bash -c prompt wrapper,\n/// and the dispatched claude subprocess (full tree, not just the tmux session).\n/// It verifies the PID is actually gone before printing success.\nfn cmd_stop(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    if !all && identifier.is_none() {\n        bail!(\"specify --all or --identifier <NAME>\");\n    }\n\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Find target sessions by name\n    let targets: Vec<TmuxSession> = if all {\n        sessions.clone()\n    } else {\n        let id = identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"\");\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.contains(id))\n            .cloned()\n            .collect()\n    };\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    for session in &targets {\n        tracing::info!(session = %session.name, \"stopping worker\");\n\n        // Get the PID from the tmux session\n        let tmux_pid = match session.pid {\n            Some(p) => p,\n            None => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: no PID found for session '{}', skipping process tree kill\",\n                    session.name\n                );\n                // Still kill the session for cleanup\n                let _ = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n                    .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", &session.name])\n                    .status();\n                continue;\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Find the actual needle run process (tmux pane_pid is the shell, not needle)\n        let needle_pid = match find_needle_process_in_tree(tmux_pid) {\n            Some(p) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    tmux_pid,\n                    needle_pid = p,\n                    \"found needle run process in process tree\"\n                );\n                p\n            }\n            None => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    tmux_pid,\n                    \"no needle run process found in tree, using tmux PID\"\n                );\n                tmux_pid\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Kill the entire process tree rooted at the needle run process\n        let killed = match kill_process_tree(needle_pid) {\n            Ok(k) => k,\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: failed to kill process tree for session '{}': {}\",\n                    session.name, e\n                );\n                false\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Verify ALL needle processes are actually gone (not just the root PID).\n        // This catches the case where new processes were spawned during the kill\n        // window or where the kill attempt didn't fully terminate the tree.\n        let remaining_processes = verify_no_needle_processes_remaining();\n        let any_remaining = !remaining_processes.is_empty();\n\n        if any_remaining {\n            println!(\n                \"Error: {} needle process(es) still running after kill attempt for session '{}':\",\n                remaining_processes.len(),\n                session.name\n            );\n            for (pid, cmdline) in &remaining_processes {\n                println!(\"  PID {}: {}\", pid, cmdline);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Kill the tmux session for cleanup\n        let kill_status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", &session.name])\n            .status();\n\n        // Clean up registry entry only if NO needle processes remain\n        if killed && !any_remaining {\n            // Extract worker identifier from session name (format: needle-<agent>-<worker_id>)\n            // Session names are sanitized: dots become underscores, so we need to handle that\n            let parts: Vec<&str> = session.name.split('-').collect();\n            let worker_id = if parts.len() >= 3 {\n                // needle-<agent>-<worker_id> -> worker_id is the third part\n                parts[2]\n            } else {\n                // Fallback: use the full session name as worker_id\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    session = %session.name,\n                    \"could not extract worker_id from session name, using full name\"\n                );\n                &session.name\n            };\n\n            let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n            let registry = Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n            if let Err(e) = registry.deregister(worker_id) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    worker_id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to deregister worker from registry\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        match (killed, any_remaining, kill_status) {\n            (true, false, Ok(s)) if s.success() => {\n                println!(\"Stopped: {} (pid {})\", session.name, needle_pid);\n            }\n            (true, false, Ok(_)) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Stopped: {} (pid {}, session already gone)\",\n                    session.name, needle_pid\n                );\n            }\n            (true, false, Err(e)) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Warning: processes killed but failed to kill session: {}\",\n                    e\n                );\n            }\n            (false, true, _) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Error: failed to stop {} (processes still running)\",\n                    session.name\n                );\n            }\n            (true, true, _) => {\n                println!(\n                    \"Error: {} - kill attempt reported success but {} process(es) still running\",\n                    session.name,\n                    remaining_processes.len()\n                );\n            }\n            (false, false, _) => {\n                println!(\"Stopped: {} (pid {} gone)\", session.name, needle_pid);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Filter sessions for cleanup based on liveness and flags.\n///\n/// This is the core filtering logic for the cleanup command, extracted to be\n/// testable. Returns the session names that should be cleaned up.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n/// * `sessions` - All discovered tmux sessions\n/// * `live_pids` - Set of PIDs that have live needle processes\n/// * `all` - If true, include all sessions regardless of liveness\n/// * `identifier` - If set, filter by identifier substring (bypasses liveness check)\n///\n/// # Returns\n/// Vector of session names to clean up\nfn filter_sessions_for_cleanup(\n    sessions: &[TmuxSession],\n    live_pids: &std::collections::HashSet<u32>,\n    all: bool,\n    identifier: &Option<String>,\n) -> Vec<String> {\n    if all {\n        // --all: remove all sessions regardless of liveness\n        sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.clone()).collect()\n    } else if let Some(id) = identifier {\n        // -i flag: filter by identifier substring (no liveness check)\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| s.name.contains(id))\n            .map(|s| s.name.clone())\n            .collect()\n    } else {\n        // Default: only orphaned sessions (no live backing process)\n        sessions\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|s| {\n                // Session is orphaned if:\n                // - It has no PID at all, OR\n                // - Its PID is not in the live process set\n                s.pid.map_or(true, |pid| !live_pids.contains(&pid))\n            })\n            .map(|s| s.name.clone())\n            .collect()\n    }\n}\n\n/// `needle cleanup` — remove orphaned tmux sessions.\n///\n/// Finds and removes needle tmux sessions that no longer have active workers.\n/// With --all, removes all needle sessions regardless of worker status.\n/// With -i, filters sessions by name/identifier substring (bypasses liveness check).\nfn cmd_cleanup(all: bool, identifier: Option<String>) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No needle sessions running.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    // Scan for live processes\n    let discovered = scan_needle_processes().unwrap_or_default();\n    let live_pids: std::collections::HashSet<u32> = discovered.iter().map(|p| p.pid).collect();\n\n    let targets = filter_sessions_for_cleanup(&sessions, &live_pids, all, &identifier);\n\n    if targets.is_empty() {\n        println!(\"No matching sessions found.\");\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cleaned = 0;\n    for session in &targets {\n        // Kill the session\n        let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n            .args([\"kill-session\", \"-t\", session])\n            .status();\n\n        match status {\n            Ok(s) if s.success() => {\n                println!(\"Cleaned up: {session}\");\n                cleaned += 1;\n            }\n            Ok(_) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: session '{session}' already gone\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                println!(\"Warning: failed to cleanup session '{session}': {e}\");\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if cleaned == 0 {\n        println!(\"No sessions cleaned up.\");\n    } else {\n        println!(\"Cleaned up {cleaned} session(s).\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle list` — show running needle sessions.\nfn cmd_list(format: ListFormat) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    // ALWAYS scan process table for ALL needle run processes (both tmux and non-tmux).\n    // This ensures we discover workers regardless of how they were started.\n    let discovered = scan_needle_processes().unwrap_or_default();\n    let tmux_pids: HashSet<u32> = sessions.iter().filter_map(|s| s.pid).collect();\n\n    // Reconciliation check: compare process table against registry\n    let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n    let registry = Registry::default_location(&config.workspace.home);\n    let _ = reconcile_process_registry(&discovered, &registry);\n\n    // Separate discovered processes into tmux and non-tmux groups\n    let _tmux_procs: Vec<&DiscoveredProcess> = discovered\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid))\n        .collect();\n    let orphaned: Vec<&DiscoveredProcess> = discovered\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|p| !tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid))\n        .collect();\n\n    if !orphaned.is_empty() {\n        tracing::warn!(\n            count = orphaned.len(),\n            pids = ?orphaned.iter().map(|p| p.pid).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            \"found needle run processes not in tmux\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Show all discovered processes, not just tmux sessions\n    if sessions.is_empty() && discovered.is_empty() {\n        match format {\n            ListFormat::Table => println!(\"No needle sessions running.\"),\n            ListFormat::Json => println!(\"[]\"),\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    match format {\n        ListFormat::Table => {\n            if !sessions.is_empty() {\n                println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", \"SESSION\", \"CREATED\", \"STATUS\");\n                println!(\"{}\", \"-\".repeat(70));\n                for s in &sessions {\n                    println!(\"{:<40} {:<20} {:<10}\", s.name, s.created, s.status);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // ALWAYS show discovered processes, even if they're in tmux\n            // This ensures visibility even if registry registration failed\n            if !discovered.is_empty() {\n                println!();\n                println!(\"Discovered Workers ({}):\", discovered.len());\n                println!(\"  All running needle run processes found via process table scan\");\n                for proc in &discovered {\n                    let workspace = proc\n                        .workspace\n                        .as_ref()\n                        .map(|p| p.display().to_string())\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"<unknown>\".to_string());\n                    let agent = proc.agent.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"<unknown>\");\n                    let identifier = proc.identifier.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"<unknown>\");\n                    let in_tmux = if tmux_pids.contains(&proc.pid) {\n                        \" (tmux)\"\n                    } else {\n                        \" (non-tmux)\"\n                    };\n                    println!(\n                        \"  PID {} — workspace: {}, agent: {}, identifier: {}{}\",\n                        proc.pid, workspace, agent, identifier, in_tmux\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Additional warning if there are orphaned processes\n            if !orphaned.is_empty() {\n                println!();\n                println!(\"  ⚠️  {} worker(s) running outside tmux (started with NEEDLE_INNER=1 or direct invocation)\", orphaned.len());\n            }\n        }\n        ListFormat::Json => {\n            let json = serde_json::json!({\n                \"tmux_sessions\": sessions,\n                \"discovered\": discovered.iter().map(|p| {\n                    serde_json::json!({\n                        \"pid\": p.pid,\n                        \"workspace\": p.workspace,\n                        \"agent\": p.agent,\n                        \"identifier\": p.identifier,\n                        \"cmdline\": p.cmdline,\n                        \"in_tmux\": tmux_pids.contains(&p.pid),\n                    })\n                }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            });\n            println!(\"{}\", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&json)?);\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle init` — initialize v2 config with optional v1 migration.\n///\n/// Creates ~/.config/needle/config.yaml. ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `needle attach <identifier>` — attach to a running worker's tmux session.\nfn cmd_attach(identifier: &str) -> Result<()> {\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions()?;\n\n    if sessions.is_empty() {\n        bail!(\"no needle sessions running\");\n    }\n\n    // Find matching session: exact match on identifier portion or substring match on full name.\n    let matches: Vec<&TmuxSession> = sessions\n        .iter()\n        .filter(|s| s.name.ends_with(&format!(\"-{identifier}\")) || s.name.contains(identifier))\n        .collect();\n\n    if matches.is_empty() {\n        let available: Vec<&str> = sessions.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"no session matching '{}'; available: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            available.join(\", \")\n        );\n    }\n\n    if matches.len() > 1 {\n        let names: Vec<&str> = matches.iter().map(|s| s.name.as_str()).collect();\n        bail!(\n            \"ambiguous identifier '{}'; matches: {}\",\n            identifier,\n            names.join(\", \")\n        );\n    }\n\n    let session = &matches[0].name;\n    let status = ProcessCommand::new(\"tmux\")\n        .args([\"attach-session\", \"-t\", session])\n        .status()\n        .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to attach to tmux session '{session}'\"))?;\n\n    if !status.success() {\n        bail!(\"tmux attach-session exited with status {status} for '{session}'\");\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// `needle status` — show fleet status summary.\nfn cmd_status(\n    format: ListFormat,\n    by_worker: bool,\n    cost: bool,\n    since: Option<String>,\n    until: Option<String>,\n    idle_strands: bool,\n) -> Result<()> {\n    let config = ConfigLoader::load_global()?;\n    let needle_home = config.workspace.home.clone();\n    let registry = Registry::default_location(&needle_home);\n    let workers = registry.list().unwrap_or_default();\n    let sessions = list_needle_sessions().unwrap_or_default();\n\n    // ALWAYS scan process table for ALL needle run processes (both registered and unregistered).\n    // This ensures we discover workers regardless of registry registration status.\n    let discovered =
